title: RunRoom DO: dispatch lease and pending-question store
description: Replace the placeholder RunRoom with the two pieces of state that are filesystem-shaped today. (1) The dispatch lease, one per project, idFromName(project): acquire returns the holder run_id on conflict rather than blocking, release is compare-and-delete so a stale holder cannot free a newer lease, and a DO alarm expires an abandoned lease. This is the SAME lease a local run takes on an enrolled project (D19) - exactly one arbiter per project. (2) The pending-question store replacing .tick/pending plus flock, with first-wins arbitration across surfaces and an already-answered-by response to losers (D5). This tick owns src/run-room.ts and is the contract three later ticks consume, so it lands alone in its wave and gets a foundation review before dependents start.

2026-08-19 19:14 - FOUNDATION REVIEW (orchestrator, read-only, before daq/ldr/kv2 build on this contract). Gate: cloud/factory vitest 100/100 (was 78), go test -short ./... clean, public-repo guard clean.

PASS — lease correctness. Compare-and-delete is real, not nominal: DispatchLeaseView is Omit<DispatchLease,'token'>, so a refused caller is never handed the holder's release credential — the one thing compare-and-delete exists to prevent, and the obvious way to get this wrong. Covered by an explicit test ('never hands a loser the holder's release token'). Race, renewal-not-conflict on re-acquire by the same run, refusal naming the holder, release-by-holder, refuse-release-by-non-holder, and alarm-based expiry of an abandoned lease are all covered.
PASS — fail-closed inputs: a ttl outside the pinned bounds is REFUSED rather than clamped, and a malformed acquire returns an error rather than throwing across RPC. Both are the right posture for a control-plane primitive; silent clamping would have made the ttl bound decorative.
PASS — D19 honoured at the schema level: LeaseOrigin is local|cloud and origin is stored and reported in the refusal detail, so one arbiter genuinely serves both a laptop run and a cloud run rather than the cloud path quietly assuming it is alone.
PASS — storage: SQLite-backed (asserted by a test reading sqlite_master), which the Phase 1 lease and pending store require and which cannot be changed after deploy.
PASS — no route-table leakage: an unknown path 404s rather than enumerating.

No blockers, no should-fix findings. Dependents may proceed. Two things for daq to inherit rather than re-derive: the refusal already carries holder run_id, epic, origin and expiry — surface that verbatim rather than re-querying — and question ids are unique-by-registration (double registration refused), so daq must not invent its own dedup.
acceptance_criteria: Two concurrent acquires yield one holder and one rejection naming it; a stale lease expires by alarm; compare-and-delete refuses to release a lease it does not hold; two surfaces answering one question yield one winner and an already-answered response; all covered in the vitest-pool-workers harness.
closed_reason: Completed: RunRoom dispatch lease (compare-and-delete release, token withheld from refused callers, alarm expiry, renewal on same-run re-acquire, bounds-checked ttl, local/cloud origin per D19) and the pending-question store with first-wins arbitration; 22 new tests, foundation review clean.
